video_title: Knicks are WINNING THE CHIP 🗣️ Stephen A. has confidence in New York finishing the job! | First Take

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen A. Smith celebrates the Knicks reaching the finals
quotes.excerpt: Start spreading the damn news. We here. We here. We here in the finals, okay? But the job's not done.
quotes.quote: What's up everybody? You see these orange and blue sky right here? Don't you see it? It could be New York City. I'm in LA right now, but I'm coming. Start spreading the damn news. We here. We here. We here in the finals, okay? But the job's not done. The job's not done, y'all. We here. Cam'ron don't look at me like that. Don't look at me like that. Shae, this ain't Chicago. Big Perk. You stay in Texas if you got to. This is what it's all about, baby. Orange and blue skies. Orange and blue skies. It's the boy in the house for the Eastern Conference Champions. Hallelujah. Whoa. Let's go.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen A. Smith questions Cam'ron's lack of Knicks enthusiasm
quotes.excerpt: The level of enthusiasm. It wasn't there. There was a bit of trepidation in this boy.

text_blocks.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
text_blocks.text: I got my receipts with me.

text_blocks.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
text_blocks.text: No, no, no, no, no, no. He did he did say that, Perk. That wasn't the way to get at Cam'ron. The way that you get at Cam'ron was that the level of enthusiasm. It wasn't there. There was a bit of trepidation in this boy. He didn't seem, he didn't seem all in. Factually, he's absolutely right. He did say the New York was going to the finals. But what he said was they they they they tend to let me down. I mean, I got him going to the finals but I hope they don't make me out to be a liar. No enthusiasm whatsoever. Well, how do you feel now?

text_blocks.speaker: Cam'ron
text_blocks.text: I don't trust the New York Knicks.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen A. Smith believes the Knicks can win the NBA Finals
quotes.excerpt: The New York Knicks will walk into the NBA finals as the clear underdog. And they will deserve it.
quotes.quote: They win they win in the chip, okay? That's where I'm going with this, right? I'm listen. The New York Knicks will walk into the NBA finals as the clear underdog. And they will deserve it because the bottom line is this. We ain't going sit up there and live behind the sky and act like the Atlanta Hawks to the play of Philadelphia 76s or the soft ass Cleveland Cavaliers or San Antonio OKC. We know better than that, okay? So we have to respect the competition. But the way that the New York Knicks have been playing, the level of production and leadership that they have gotten from the likes of Jalen Brunson and Karl-Anthony Towns. I got to give Mikal Bridges love. Listen, I've been on them. I would like to remind America and the basketball world that the New York Knicks have not lost since. They have not lost since. I was getting on Mikal Bridges, they haven't lost since. The brothers averaging over 18, shooting 57% from the field, flat out balling, very, very proud of them, very proud of them, very proud of OG. Very proud, damn it, I'm proud. You see that basketball. This is the kind of stuff that I'm talking about. The way that the New York Knicks are playing basketball. It obviously has to continue, but in all seriousness fellas, here's what I'm loving.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Kendrick Perkins explains why he picked the Knicks to reach the finals
quotes.excerpt: They added depth to their roster. That was the biggest thing. That was the one thing that was lacking.

text_blocks.speaker: Cam'ron
text_blocks.text: Stephen A., we're in court. Thank you for your answer. Big Perk, why did you pick the Knicks?

text_blocks.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
text_blocks.text: Well, one because they they added depth to their roster. That was the biggest thing. They had a depth and I was like that was the one thing that was lacking. And then outside of going to get Mike Brown, I knew he was going to come in and be a new voice, but you look at the Eastern conference and obviously looking at Jayson Tatum being sidelined, I was saying to myself, well who else is in their way? I didn't come into this season trusting the Cavs. Now I will say this, it was a point of time where the Celtics were looking like the favorites and I did at the point of time. I did switch and say, man, I believe that the Celtics are coming out of the East, but I never really doubted the Knicks. I got on them at times but I never doubted them. But go ahead, keep going. This ain't a Q&A. This ain't a Q&A.

quotes.speaker: Cam'ron
quotes.summary_phrase: Cam'ron says Knicks' success was expected but doubts their finals win
quotes.excerpt: This is what was supposed to happen. Where everything you all named is exactly why I thought the Knicks was going to the finals.

text_blocks.speaker: Cam'ron
text_blocks.text: The reason I'm asking the show how you're doing. I get to speak before the show. Is what you'll predicted this? This is this is what was supposed to happen. Tyrese Haliburton hurt. Jayson Tatum hurt. Damian Lillard got shipped out. Now the way the Knicks are winning is crazy. We're not going to act like they're not set in history. 11 games or 12 it was 11 games straight right now. 11 games straight by average of nearly 20. 47 points in half time against Atlanta. Absolutely. I totally agree with you. But this is what was supposed to happen. Where everything you all named is exactly why I thought the Knicks was going to the finals. And all you Knicks fans, stop tagging me. I said you all was going to the finals. It's about what you do when you get to the finals. So yes, the Knicks are playing exceptionally well. I'm happy that they got there. But no, I do not trust the Knicks yet to win the finals. The level of competition that they're going to face in the finals is not going to be the level the competition they face in the Eastern conference. Now what I will say is they're going to have a lot of rest. A whole lot of rest because I believe that the San Antonio OKC series is going seven games. But no, not until four games are won. Now, I do like their body language. I like Jalen Brunson setting the tone. It's no celebrations, it's no smiles, it's black glasses, black skullies after the after the interviews. I like how he's setting the tone. No, I don't trust it yet. Get, make all the faces you want. Get.

text_blocks.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
text_blocks.text: Well, I do I do trust the Knicks.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Kendrick Perkins trusts the Knicks to win the NBA championship
quotes.excerpt: The Knicks has been the best basketball team in this post season, offensively and defensively in my opinion.
quotes.quote: Well, I do I do trust the Knicks and I believe that they do have a real shot at winning the NBA championship. The Knicks has been the best basketball team in this post season, offensively and defensively in my opinion, the way that they've been tied together like shoe laces, the chemistry on both ends of the floor. They check all the boxes, Cam, all the boxes to win the championship. They have a closer in Big Body Brunson, who by the way, has now become in my opinion, the best player in the Eastern conference. You have Karl-Anthony Towns, who is the top three big in the NBA and has shown the world that he could slide his feet and be a defensive anchor defensively while picking up dumb fouls. And you know the most important thing that they have? They have a lot of two-way players. Guess what? The Knicks got two-way players. When you talk about OG Anunoby, Josh Hart, Mikal Bridges, even McBride at this point, Landry Shamet, they are deep. Big Mitchell Robinson coming in off the bench, so they're deep at the center position. I don't know what you've been watching, and I get it, we could sit up here and downplay the level of play the level of competition in the Eastern conference, but I'm not going to do that. Because how the Knicks has been performing and dominating, this team is physical, they're about their life and the most important thing that I saw last night was that the celebration wasn't too much. They did a little bit, but when they came into their post game interviews, they had something on their mind. It was a different type of spirit. Some people be happy to get to the finals and when you happy and satisfied is when you get when you take L's like we saw with the Cleveland Cavaliers. But make no mistake about it. This team checked all the boxes to go and compete against OKC and the San Antonio Spurs and they have a legit shot at beating both of those teams.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen A. Smith says Knicks are finally meeting expectations after decades
quotes.excerpt: He has no sensitivity whatsoever to the suffering that has transpired since 1973.

text_blocks.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
text_blocks.text: Let me say this to Cam, to the American people out there that especially the ones that have been harassing Cam, with the DMs, whatever the hell they're doing with you.

text_blocks.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
text_blocks.text: Keep on doing it. Harass his ass all day long. Harass him, don't stop. You understand. Don't stop. Keep harassing him, okay? Because here's the reality of the situation, all right? Cam is from New York City. And what he does is he has no sensitivity whatsoever. It's very inexplicable. He has no sensitivity whatsoever to the suffering that has transpired since 1973. We ain't won since 1973. You talk about we were supposed to happen. How many things over the decades were supposed to happen that didn't happen when the New York Knicks?

text_blocks.speaker: Cam'ron
text_blocks.text: That's my problem, Stephen A. That's the problem.

text_blocks.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
text_blocks.text: That's the point that I'm saying to you. The point that I'm saying to you is that they finally did something that they were supposed to do. They were supposed to get to the finals and they did it.

text_blocks.speaker: Cam'ron
text_blocks.text: You felt the Knicks were going to win around this time 94. How did you feel?

text_blocks.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
text_blocks.text: In 94? In 94, I felt like Houston was going to be tough, but I thought they could take Houston.

text_blocks.speaker: Cam'ron
text_blocks.text: You felt like this before the season started, before the championship started?

text_blocks.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
text_blocks.text: Absolutely because Jordan had retired. So when the New York Knicks got to the finals, they did what they were supposed to do and we was excited. We were excited about it because we said, yo, you got Elijah, Juan and Thorp and Kenny Smith and the crew, I got that, but we got Ewing. We got the crew. And if Pat Riley, we love Pat Riley, but if Pat Riley had remembered you acquired Rolando Blackman to put him into the damn game for perimeter shooting. Had he remembered that? We had the one the damn championship as far as I'm concerned. So that's how I look at it. But the point is, you look at the New York Knicks right now, doing what you're supposed to do is the first time that's happened in nearly 40 years. All right, that matters, damn it.
